- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility clustering.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.0), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply decay factor or cap forecast at +5–10% above peak.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 2–4 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >75.0, reduce by 0.5–1.0 per day until convergence to 70–74 range.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore volatility; increase forecast variance or add stochastic noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 18-day trend, not 30-day trend.
